1. The hole-related models differ from one another only within the hole by diffeomorphic mathematical description.
2. Leibniz equivalence holds that diffeomorphic models represent the same physical situation.
3. The hole-related models are models of a local spacetime theory.
4. Leibniz equivalence is a principle of physical equivalence.
5. If X is a principle of physical equivalence and Y are models of a local spacetime theory and X holds that diffeomorphic models represent the same physical situation and Y differ from one another only within the hole by diffeomorphic mathematical description, then under X Y represent the same physical situation.
6. Therefore, under Leibniz equivalence the hole-related models represent the same physical situation. [1,2,3,4,5]
7. The radical local indeterminism arises from treating the hole-related models as representing distinct physical situations.
8. If X is a principle of physical equivalence and Y are models of a local spacetime theory and under X Y represent the same physical situation and the radical local indeterminism arises from treating Y as representing distinct physical situations, then accepting X transforms the radical local indeterminism into an underdetermination of mathematical description with no corresponding underdetermination of the physical situation.
9. Therefore, accepting Leibniz equivalence transforms the radical local indeterminism into an underdetermination of mathematical description with no corresponding underdetermination of the physical situation. [3,4,6,7,8]
10. If X is a principle of physical equivalence and accepting X transforms the radical local indeterminism into an underdetermination of mathematical description with no corresponding underdetermination of the physical situation, then accepting X removes the radical local indeterminism.
11. Therefore, accepting Leibniz equivalence removes the radical local indeterminism. [4,9,10]
